chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī narrated from al-Faḍl ibn al-Mubārak al-Baṣrī, from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him, "May I be your ransom, a man is obligated to free a believing slave, but he cannot find one. What should he do?"
He عليه السلام said, "Resort to the children and free them. If they turn out to be believing, then that is it; and if they do not turn out to be believing, then there is nothing upon you."

key_terms.رَقَبَةٍ: a slave person to be freed in expiation or obligation
key_terms.عِتْقُ: the act of emancipation or manumission
key_terms.ٱلْأَطْفَالِ: children; here referring to young slaves

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if freeing a believing slave is obligatory but no believing slave can be found?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who is required to free a believing slave but cannot find such a person. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام instructs that children may be emancipated in such a case, and if they later prove to be believers the obligation is fulfilled; otherwise, no liability remains upon the one who freed them.
